summary: Downtown Okanogan rooftop firefinder, documented from 1930; the roof lookout is gone and the building still stands as a store.

facts.design: Firefinder on the roof of a downtown Okanogan post office building (1930s)
facts.status_note: The roof firefinder is gone (abandoned in the 1940s, per firelookout.com). The building it sat on still stands downtown and now houses a department store.

access.note: Street-level stop at 2nd Avenue and Queen Street in downtown Okanogan. The building is a store; the sources do not say whether the roof can be reached.

visit.trail_note: Drive-up on a paved road (Willhite); pair with the Okanogan Historical Walk and county museum (TrailChick)

events.note: Lookout on the post office roof: 1930 panoramic photo and an inventory entry. Kresek's 2014 note says the photo shows only that a lookout was proposed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The roof lookout is gone: firelookout.com says abandoned in the 1940s and Forest Lookouts says removed. Sources calling it 'still standing' (TrailChick, SummitPost) refer to the building, which still stands and is now a store.
860 feet on firelookout.com and Willhite; TrailChick gives 800 feet. The record keeps 860 feet (262.1 m).

notes_for_editor: Whether a lookout ever stood on the roof is disputed. Kresek's 2014 note (quoted on SummitPost) says the 1930 photo only proves a lookout was proposed; the inventory entry says 'had a lookout'; Willhite and TrailChick accept it. The story reports both. Building identity is unresolved: the record name 'Okanogan P.O.' is the post office, but a 2014 note quoted on SummitPost puts the lookout on the First National Bank building, now part of Rawson's. The record name may need a note. No source gives a year for removal; firelookout says abandoned in the 1940s, so no dated event was added. Access changed from 'unknown' to 'public' (street-level store; roof access not addressed). The brief's 'standing' conflicts refer to the building. The SummitPost note's author is unnamed in the source and is not named here. Budget: 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads; the Okanogan Country page repeated TrailChick and was not cited.
